final.answer: The plug seal rings for the FV-21-3 valve are available in several materials, with temperature limits depending on the specific material and seal design. PTFE is suitable from –73 to 204 °C / –100 to 400 °F. PTFE with N10276 spring and Carbon-filled PTFE are rated from –73 to 232 °C / –100 to 450 °F. PTFE/graphite with R30003 spring can handle –73 to 316 °C / –100 to 600 °F, though this is limited to 260 °C / 500 °F for oxidizing service. UHMWPE R30003 is available for –198 to 66 °C / –325 to 150 °F (with 316 SST/ENC cage) or –29 to 66 °C / –20 to 150 °F (with 17-4 SST cage). For temperatures above 232 °C / 450 °F, PEEK anti-extrusion rings plus a spring-loaded seal ring are required, allowing the valve to reach 316 °C / 600 °F in non-oxidizing service or 260 °C / 500 °F in oxidizing service.

How to check: the ET valve comes in a standard PTFE-seat design (with a metal disk seat, PTFE disk and disk retainer), an optional metal-seat design (metal seat ring/liner), and balanced TSO trim with a valve plug seal and protected soft seat. If the valve is a standard PTFE-seat ET, leakage through when shut is most likely at the PTFE disk/seat ring interface — inspect the PTFE disk and seat ring for damage or wear, and verify the shutoff class (per ANSI/FCI 70-2 / IEC 60534-4, Table 4). If it is a balanced TSO trim valve, the leak path can also be the valve plug seal (seal ring, backup ring, retaining ring) — inspect the plug seal components. Also check the trim cartridge/trim number on the valve to identify which seat and seal parts are fitted, since trim materials and seat types vary by trim number (e.g. Table 8, Table 7 for Class VI trims).
